observations: Main route has only 35 boxes, 19 of them explosives; the bonus holds 49 (29 iron-bound).
Every enemy is paired with an explosive or a box.
The only Aku box is inside the hardest fire-timing stretch.
A ! that arms Nitros and a green ! reachable only by enemy bounce make the perfect a behavioural count trap.
The optional gem course has zero boxes, separating completionist and gem goals.
Bonus is a slam-order puzzle: notch entry, ? caps, TNT lit from the top of what it clears.

cameraSections.notes: diagonal climb from the start pipe (bottom-left) to the top-right (F2 p071R lower half): a chain of pillar tops, hex pads and a narrow walkway over a void.
continues up and right (F2 p071R upper half) along ledges on columns to the ! room, then a narrow walkway straight into the screen to C2.
gorilla log alleys along chains of platforms (D2 p062 shots 14–17, p063 18–30); logs come toward the camera.
single-lane walkways, a rotating ring and pillar clusters climbing to C3 (F2 p072L).
the route doubles back up and to the left (F2 p072R lower half, つづき← then つづく↑).
turns right along the top strip (F2 p072R): the rat ring, then a stepped pillar line down to the gorilla and the goal.
a flat room left to right (D2 p064 shots 39–44).

geometryObservations: The level runs on two opposite pressures. Fire statues say "wait" and the floors say "don't": crumbling tiles, a crumbling ledge, tilting pillars and a rotating ring. Its hardest beats put both on one lane (O-S3-c), and POINT6 sums it up: hesitate and you are burnt.

The statue lesson is ordered. First comes a single statue beside a standing start (O-S1-a), then a single statue beside a hop chain (O-S1-b). Next is a pair flanking a lane with a solid floor (O-S3-a: wait for both), and finally pairs over crumbling tiles with a safe pad between them (O-S3-c). There are 8 statues on the main route: 2 singles and 3 pairs.

Walls mark rest. Every checkpoint sits on a walled square platform (parapets on three sides), and these are almost the only edges you cannot fall off. Everything else is open-edged over a void, so rest is readable from the geometry alone.

Lanes are one tile wide (≈1.5 u) wherever enemies patrol: the lizard walkway, the monkey walkway and the TNT ledge. The lane makes the enemy unavoidable and makes the lengthwise slide the right tool (POINT2).

Enemies are tools or triggers more often than obstacles. A rat is a stepping stone between Nitros (E-S4-a), and a monkey's return times your exit from a lit TNT (E-S2-b). A lizard walks into its own TNT (E-S4-b), rats carry you up to the green ! (E-S5-a), and one rat should not be killed because it releases a lizard (E-S1-b).

Perspective is a deliberate test. The into-screen camera looks along pillar chains, and D2 19 says the jumps only look long. POINT8 asks the player to grasp the depth on tilted pillars, and F2 p099R warns that the gem course's diagonal jumps are hard to judge. Gaps stay ≈1–2 u wide so that a plain jump is nearly always enough, once trusted.

Moving platforms serve as both transport and gate. The rotating hex ring carries you to the bonus pad (P-S3-b). The rotating rat ring around the floating green ! is the climax, because there the moving platform delivers the enemy you must bounce on (P-S5-a).

Explosives are geometry. TNT stacks fill a narrow ledge, so you must land on them and race their fuse (G-S2-b). Nitros on a crumbling ledge combine a floor you cannot wait on with crates you cannot touch (G-S2-c). Nitros bracket a rat so that the enemy becomes the bridge (G-S4-a).

The gorilla alleys use a projectile to set the rhythm: wait for the log, jump two platforms, wait again (G-GEM-a, G-S5-b). The same cadence opens the gem course and closes the main route, so every player meets it once.

The gem course remixes the theme at its hardest. It has crumble rows, collapsing hexes, tilting pillars, a statue beside a crumble row and three gorillas, but it names its breather platforms explicitly (D2 23, 25) and holds no boxes. It is a pure skill route.

Recovery is ungenerous in geometry (nearly every gap is bottomless) and generous in rests and help. Each checkpoint is walled, the Aku pad sits inside the statue gauntlet, and loose masks wait above the steel arrow and beside the green !.

Difficulty comes from timing couplings rather than from gap length or enemy count. Fire, crumble, tilt, rotation, logs and fuses each modulate gaps that rarely exceed 2 u. A designer can build every section from one short gap plus one timer.
geometryTransfer: Fire lane: put a pair of `firetiki` heads (cycle/phase offset so their windows overlap briefly) on either side of a one-crate-wide walkway (≈1.2–1.7 m). Floor it with `crumble` tiles (short `shake`, ≈0.3 s) in two halves, and place a walled 2–3-crate safe pad (≈2.3–3.5 m) between the halves with a mask on it. On foot the lane is ≈8–10 crates (≈9–12 m), roughly 1–1.3 s of running at 9 m/s, so the shared fire window must be at least that long.

Tilting-pillar crossing: there is no tilt primitive, so use two `mover` pads (≈1.7–2.3 m tops) oscillating on `axis: "x"` toward each other. The gap should open and close between ≈1.7 and ≈2.9 m (1.5–2.5 crates): always inside a full jump (≈5.6 m), but only comfortable for a tap jump at the narrowest point. That teaches "jump when they are closest".

Log alley: line up five 1.5-crate pillars (≈1.7 m) with ≈2-crate gaps (≈2.3 m) and roll a `stone` along the line toward the player (default axis Z), with its speed and range tuned so one boulder passes every two jumps. Put a `sentry` or a `charger` on the last pad as the thrower or gatekeeper.

Walled checkpoints in open levels: in a level built on open-edged pillars over a `pit`, give every checkpoint pad a one-crate parapet on three sides, so rest is visible at a glance. For skaters, the parapet tops are ledges that grind by default.

Enemy-bounce switch: float a green ! about 4–5 m up over a `pit`, beyond the double-jump reach (≈4.6 m). Circle it with stompable `grunt`s riding `mover` pads, because a stomp bounce (≈3 m) plus a double jump reaches it. Put the checkpoint on the boarding pad, as Crash does at C4.
